subject: apollo-11
title: Footprints on the Moon
summary: The day people first walked on the Moon, and the thousands who made it happen.

keys.prompt: Only two people walked on the Moon in 1969. How many did Armstrong say made it work?
keys.answer: Hundreds of thousands. It took a giant team.

keys.prompt: Why did Armstrong steer the lander Eagle by hand?
keys.answer: To fly past a field of big boulders. They landed with only about 30 seconds of fuel left.

options.text: To get past a field of big boulders
Because the rocket was too tall

cards.title: 30 seconds to spare
cards.text: When the first spaceship to carry people landed on the Moon, it had only about 30 seconds of fuel left. What happened in those last tense minutes?

cards.question: Only two people walked on the Moon in 1969. How many people do you think helped make it happen?
cards.reveal: Armstrong said "hundreds of thousands" of people made the mission work. Each one tried hard to make sure nothing went wrong because of them.

cards.title: The big rocket
cards.text: On July 16, 1969, three astronauts blasted off from Florida on a Saturn V rocket. It was 363 feet tall. That is taller than a football field is long!
cards.example: The crew was Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins.

cards.title: The Eagle has landed
cards.text: Four days later, Armstrong and Aldrin flew a small lander called Eagle down to the Moon. Collins stayed in orbit in the main ship, Columbia. Armstrong steered by hand past a field of big boulders. Then he radioed, "The Eagle has landed."

cards.title: One small step
cards.text: That night, Armstrong climbed down the ladder and stepped onto the Moon. He said, "That's one small step for a man, one giant leap for mankind." More than half a billion people watched on TV.
cards.example: Aldrin joined him. They explored for about two and a half hours, collected rocks, and took photos.

cards.title: A giant team
cards.text: Years later, Armstrong said "hundreds of thousands" of people made the mission work. Each one tried hard to make sure nothing went wrong because of them. The crew splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean on July 24.

why.q: Why would each person on the team care so much about their own job?
why.a: Armstrong said each one tried hard to make sure nothing went wrong because of them. Every small job mattered.

cards.question: Only two people walked on the Moon that day, but hundreds of thousands helped. Why do you think so many people were needed? Who gets the credit?
nudges: Think about everything a trip to the Moon needs.
Is there a job you do on a team that nobody sees?

questions.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?

options.why: Yes! Buzz Aldrin followed him about 20 minutes later.
Collins stayed in orbit around the Moon in Columbia.
Aldrin was second. Armstrong went first.

questions.q: What did Armstrong do when Eagle was about to land?

options.text: He steered by hand past big boulders.
options.why: Right. That used up fuel, so they landed with about 30 seconds left.

options.text: He turned around and went home.
options.why: He kept going and landed safely.

options.text: He let the computer do everything.
options.why: He took over and steered by hand.

questions.q: How many people did Armstrong say helped the mission?

options.why: Yes. It took a giant team.
Three astronauts flew, but many more people made it work.
Way more! He said hundreds of thousands.

sources.supports: Kennedy's 1961 goal; crew roles; launch July 16, 1969; an estimated 650 million viewers; landing about four miles downrange after maneuvering to avoid a crater; 21 hours 36 minutes on the surface; experiments left behind; splashdown July 24 after 195 hours, 18 minutes.
